This is a guide to reviewing the refactor, rather than a new user tutorial.
The public functions, defaults and 56-slot saved object remain the interface.
The refactor adds no SPA, Wilcoxon, accelerated fitter, new QC rule, backend or
backed CRT. The lasting reference is [ARCHITECTURE.md](../../ARCHITECTURE.md).
This temporary walkthrough and comparison harness live with the code in Git,
but are excluded from the R source package and permanent CI.

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
root <- normalizePath("../..", mustWork = TRUE)
stopifnot(file.exists(file.path(root, "R/analysis_context.R")))
# Display actual source, not a second hand-maintained version of the code.
show_function <- function(file, name) {
    expressions <- parse(file.path(root, file), keep.source = TRUE)
    refs <- attr(expressions, "srcref")
    hit <- which(vapply(expressions, function(x) {
        is.call(x) && identical(x[[1L]], as.name("<-")) &&
            identical(x[[2L]], as.name(name))
    }, logical(1)))
    stopifnot(length(hit) == 1L)
    lines <- readLines(file.path(root, file))
    span <- refs[[hit]]
    cat("```r\n", paste(lines[span[[1L]]:span[[3L]]], collapse = "\n"),
        "\n```\n", sep = "")
}
```

## Start with the ownership map

The former large analysis and numerical routines mixed cell selection, storage,
fitting, sampling, execution and result processing. The new responsibilities
are concrete modules with ordinary inputs. The S4 object remains the workflow
facade and saved state; it is not passed through every numerical operation.

| Concern | Start reading here | Key boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Workflow checks and state commit | `R/s4_analysis_functs_2.R`, `R/workflow_state.R` | Commit successful outputs/cache |
| Analysis preparation | `R/analysis.R`, `R/analysis_context.R` | Transient context and ordered views |
| Sparse/backed access | `R/storage.R` | Source row and source-cell positions |
| QC measurements and rule | `R/pair_qc.R`, `src/pair_eligibility.h` | Measurements separate from the shared predicate |
| Response/assignment fits | `R/fitting.R` | Aligned response/design to compact fit/probabilities |
| Scores and fit reuse | `R/score_preparation.R`, `R/fit_cache.R` | Array orientation and explicit invalidation |
| Association traversal | `R/association_execution.R`, `R/association_workers.R` | Different permutation/CRT reuse scopes |
| Worker dispatch | `R/execution.R` | Partitioning, logs, collection |
| Native inference | `src/inference_scores.cpp`, `src/inference_tail.cpp`, `src/inference_stages.cpp` | Scores, selected null segments, stages, R conversion |
| Result processing | `R/result_processing.R` | Requested rows, guide integration, complete-family correction |

The split does not create a generic plugin framework. A later extension should
change the few concrete owners it needs and add its own scientific validation.

## Trace one discovery association

1. `run_discovery_analysis()` checks workflow prerequisites and owns successful
   state/cache writeback.
2. `analyze_association_pairs()` prepares eligible requests and a transient
   analysis context. Each request keeps its identity independently of traversal.
3. `run_permutation_analysis()` traverses responses and shares the full run's
   permutation bank. `run_crt_analysis()` prepares response fits, then traverses
   guides and shares one assignment model/full bank across that guide's responses.
4. Workers read aligned counts and design through the same cell view, obtain
   the applicable shared or guide-specific fit, and prepare the score arrays.
5. The checked `run_association_test()` Rcpp boundary converts observed R
   positions once. Private numerical components calculate the effect, score and
   selected tail/stage. Synthetic draw positions are already zero based.
6. `pair_results_from_native()` converts native records. `assemble_pair_results()`
   restores failed-QC requests. Finalization integrates guides and applies the
   correction over the complete analysis family. Nuclear pipeline shards remain
   raw; the collector owns the corresponding complete-family operation.

Keep the two traversals distinct: a single universal loop would hide where
fitting and sampling can safely be reused. NT-control discovery needs its own
treatment-plus-NT fits; an all-cell fit cannot silently replace them.

## Indexing: source, analysis, fit

Source positions are original matrix columns. Analysis positions index the
ordered retained-cell map. Fit positions index a particular ordered view.
All three use **one-based R positions**; native draw banks use zero-based fit
positions. Saved legacy NT-local assignments are decoded once at preparation.

The following example executes the actual private view functions directly from
this checkout. It does not load an installed package, open backing files or fit
a model.

```{r}
#| label: ordered-cell-view
context_code <- new.env(parent = baseenv())
sys.source(file.path(root, "R/analysis_context.R"), envir = context_code)
index <- list(
    analysis_to_source = c(2L, 4L, 5L, 8L, 11L),
    groups_analysis = list(A = c(2L, 3L)),
    nt_to_analysis = c(4L, 1L, 5L),
    calibration_check = FALSE,
    control_group_complement = FALSE
)
view <- context_code$make_fit_view(index, "A")
view
stopifnot(identical(view$source_cells, c(4L, 5L, 8L, 2L, 11L)),
          identical(view$trt_fit_pos, 1:2))
```

The response row and design select source columns `4, 5, 8, 2, 11` in that order.
Observed treatment positions are `1, 2` inside this fit, not `4, 5`.
The code that constructs that view is included directly below.

```{r}
#| label: view-source
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
show_function("R/analysis_context.R", "make_fit_view")
```

Raw source membership uses set membership in analysis order. It must not use
the incoming vector's ordering as the fitted-cell order:

```{r}
context_code$source_membership_to_analysis(c(5L, 4L, 5L),
                                         index$analysis_to_source)
# Analysis positions 2 and 3, with duplicates removed.
```

Review `tests/testthat/test-refactor-indexing.R` for independently specified
ordering, noncontiguous cells and observed/synthetic coordinate tests.

## A small fitting boundary

`fit_response()` accepts an expression vector and an aligned matrix design.
It owns the existing Poisson fit and clipped dispersion estimate; it does not
select cells, read storage, schedule work or commit a cache. Score preparation
is a separate owner.

```{r}
#| label: fitter-source
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
show_function("R/fitting.R", "fit_response")
```

A future GLMGamPoi-style replacement can start here, but must decide compatible
fit outputs, warnings and numerical behavior. Effective fitter/settings changes
also require cache-identity review and scientific validation. This refactor does
not choose those definitions or claim any acceleration.

## Where extensions would enter

| Possible later work | Owners to inspect | Work still required later |
|---|---|---|
| Faster response fitting | `fitting.R`, `score_preparation.R`, `fit_cache.R` | Fit/score compatibility, cache identity, statistical and resource checks |
| SPA or Wilcoxon | Association workers and result conversion | Define method inputs/results; avoid unnecessary current score/draw work |
| Pairwise QC replacement | `pair_qc.R`, `pair_eligibility.h`, calibration candidate construction | Define measurements and a rule shared by discovery and calibration |
| Bioconductor-backed data | Import boundary and `storage.R` | Representation semantics, ordering, shapes, nonmutation and I/O validation |
| Backed CRT | Storage, CRT plan, existing validation guard, pipeline | Validate one assignment bank per guide/view, fit access and resource behavior before relaxing the guard |
| New outcome models | Fitter/score/test boundaries and workflow validation | Specify model and inferential meaning rather than forcing it into count-model assumptions |
| Nextflow changes | Compatibility entrypoints and collector | Respect raw shard schemas and global correction; run real consumers |

`ondisc` is a separate package/dependency boundary. Its private calls are isolated
in storage; this does not establish that ondisc needs no future work or change
its own API. Existing backed CRT remains unsupported.

## Review and compare

Normal package CI checks the **current package**. It has no old SCEPTRE bootstrap,
reference oracle or historical output comparison. Permanent tests retain
mathematical contracts, indexing, nonmutation, current cache behavior,
serial/fork and sparse/backed parity, and current saved-object roundtrips.
`tools/checks/` contains current-source mathematical and controlled native
error-boundary probes. Both developer directories are build-excluded.

For the separate refactor-specific comparison, from a committed checkout run:

```bash
Rscript --vanilla tools/refactor/compare.R /absolute/fresh/output
```

The optional second argument selects a candidate commit/ref; default `HEAD`.
Uncommitted changes are not included. The command archives both refs into the
output directory, installs the candidate freshly, verifies and runs the original
in a separate R process with matching dependencies, then executes the relocated
historical suite against the installed candidate. It neither updates expected
outputs from candidate code nor installs missing developer dependencies.
See [the command guide](consistency/README.md) for dependencies and output files.

Read the pinned refs and status in `comparison.json`, then `checks.csv` and logs.
The manual suite covers public inventories, saved-object compatibility, workflows,
QC/ordering/budgets/cache observations, prepared numerical stages and full
same-environment production sampler banks. A platform-specific archived-stream
check may skip on another toolchain; the source-stream comparison still runs.
Failures return nonzero and retain logs.

This one command does not certify actual Nextflow, selected book examples or
performance. [FINAL_ACCEPTANCE.md](FINAL_ACCEPTANCE.md) binds those earlier
qualifications to their measured source commits. It also records the separately
accepted eight-million-entry conversion memory cost and Papalexi cold serial
peak increase from about 505 to 667 MiB. The latter's cause remains unresolved.
This tooling separation does not change production code or remeasure those costs.

## What to keep later

Keep `ARCHITECTURE.md`, permanent tests and current-source CI checks with SCEPTRE.
Retain this walkthrough, manual comparison and historical evidence for Tim's
review. After acceptance, preserve a tagged snapshot before retiring
`tools/refactor/`; deleting it is a separate maintainer decision.
